The backup withholding rate is 24% for reportable payments.
A payor must deduct, withhold, and deposit with IRS 24% of reportable payments made to that payee until the cause of the backup withholding is remedied.
If an account holder fails to provide its TIN, then the withholding rate is 30%.
must withhold a tax equal to 10% of the amount realized, unless an exception applies
The payee has 60 calendar days, from the date you receive this certificate, to provide a TIN.
You must backup withhold on any reportable payments made during the 60-day period if a payee withdraws more than $500 at one time
Treat as reportable payments all cash withdrawals in an amount up to the reportable payments made from the day after you receive the awaiting-TIN certificate to the day of withdrawal.
The 60-day exemption from backup withholding does not apply to any payment other than interest, dividends, and certain payments relating to readily tradable instruments.
A recalcitrant account holder is an account holder that is not an FFI and that fails to comply with documentation or information requests from an FFI in which it holds an account.
If several persons qualify as withholding agents for a single payment, the tax must only be withheld once.

notes: IRS instructions PDF exactly as served (7 pages, US Letter, two columns, Rev. March 2024; page-1 footer 'Mar 11, 2024' and 'Cat. No. 20479P'; the PDF is tagged). Page 1 has the title block across both columns ('Instructions for the Requester of Form W-9', '(Rev. March 2024)', bold subtitle 'Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification') and the Treasury/IRS logo. Headings: the title and the 21 large bold section headings, each written as printed (several wrap over two lines). 'What’s New' is a section heading too but is not listed: its apostrophe is typographic and its code point cannot be seen. Bold run-in paragraph labels ('Line 3a.', 'Backup withholding rate.', 'Reserve rule.', 'Form 945.' ...) and the italic 'Option 1.'/'Option 2.' are body text, not headings. 'Purpose' is a whole heading line; the heading 'Establishing U.S. Status for Purposes ...' also contains it, and the one-to-one heading match keeps the two apart. The file has no tables (lists only), so tables is empty. must_contain: 22 phrases, each printed once, none with an apostrophe or quotation mark, none crossing a column or page break; 'A trust exempt from tax under section 664 or described in section 4947' is printed twice (items 13 and L) and is not used. Several headings and two phrases contain 'W-9', '60-day', 'awaiting-TIN' or 'tax-exempt' with a hyphen written as ASCII hyphen-minus (the blind protocol could not confirm the code point). ordered: 8 body-text anchors on pages 1 (left, right), 2 (left, right), 3, 4, 5 and 7. Noise (visible furniture): the footer 'Instr. for Req. of Form W-9 (Rev. 3-2024)' is printed on pages 2-7 (6 times), max 1; page numbers are too short to count. Absent: the text is mostly ragged-right; the only one-word line-end hyphenation seen is the bold run-in 'Payments made in settlement of payment card or third par-' / 'ty network transactions.' on page 5, listed as its split form. BLIND PROTOCOL: chosen and answered before any converter or text extractor was run on the file; every check was typed from the rendered pages (pdftoppm at 150-300 dpi, read as images), and the PDF text layer was never read. Consequences: (1) text that may be an image (logos, mastheads, cover art, chart labels) is not checked; (2) invisible text-layer content cannot be known, so noise lists only VISIBLE repeated page furniture; (3) where the exact code point of a glyph cannot be seen (curly vs straight quotes, dash and minus variants, the '>=' sign), must_contain phrases and ordered anchors avoid it; headings, table cells and absent entries that cannot avoid it are noted per file.
